question.text: If $\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{96 x^2 \cos ^2 x}{\left(1+e^x\right)} \mathrm{d} x=\pi\left(\alpha \pi^2+\beta\right), \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$, then $(\alpha+\beta)^2$ equals

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & I=\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{96 x^2 \cos ^2 x}{1+e^x} d x \\ & 2 I=2 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 96 x^2 \cos ^2 x d x \\ & I=96 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} x^2 \cos ^2 x d x \\ & =48 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} x^2(1+\cos 2 x) d x \\ & =2 \pi^2+48(0-0)-48 \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} x \sin 2 x d x \\ & =2 \pi^2-12 \pi+[0-0]=\pi\left(2 \pi^2-12\right) \\ & =\pi\left(\alpha \pi^2+\beta\right) \\ & \Rightarrow(\alpha+\beta)^2=100\end{aligned}$
